{{Short description|Stability conditions for triangulated cateogires}}
In [[mathematics]], and especially [[algebraic geometry]], a '''Bridgeland stability condition''' is an algebro-geometric stability condition defined on elements of a [[triangulated category]]. Stability conditions serve a two-fold purpose in the theory - first, the space of all stability conditions on the triangulated category carries the structure of a [[complex manifold]], thus furnishing an [[Invariant (mathematics)|invariant]] of the category that is topological in nature. Second, each stability condition allows the construction of well-behaved [[moduli space]]s parametrising objects in the category that are semistable with respect to it.

The case of original interest and particular importance is when this triangulated category is the [[derived category]] of [[coherent sheaves]] on a [[Calabi–Yau manifold]], and this situation has fundamental links to [[string theory]] and the study of [[D-brane]]s. Such stability conditions were introduced in a rudimentary form by [[Michael R. Douglas|Michael Douglas]] called <math>\Pi</math>-stability and used to study [[Bogomol'nyi–Prasad–Sommerfield state|BPS]] B-branes in string theory.<ref name=douglas>Douglas, M.R., Fiol, B. and Römelsberger, C., 2005. Stability and BPS branes. Journal of High Energy Physics, 2005(09), p. 006.</ref> This concept was made precise by [[Tom Bridgeland]], who defined stability conditions and initiated their study mathematically,<ref name="bridgeland">{{cite arXiv |last=Bridgeland |first=Tom |date=2006-02-08 |title=Stability conditions on triangulated categories |eprint=math/0212237 }}</ref> and after whom the concept is named.

(Bridgeland) stability conditions remain an active area of research. The moduli spaces they furnish have yielded new constructions of [[Hyperkähler manifold|hyperKähler]] varieties,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bayer |first1=Arend |title=Stability conditions in families |date=2022-01-25 |arxiv=1902.08184 |last2=Lahoz |first2=Martí |last3=Macrì |first3=Emanuele |last4=Nuer |first4=Howard |last5=Perry |first5=Alexander |last6=Stellari |first6=Paolo |journal=Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS |volume=133 |pages=157–325 |doi=10.1007/s10240-021-00124-6 }}</ref> and the ''stability manifold'' (i.e. the complex manifold formed by all stability conditions) has been used to study the [[Equivalence of categories|autoequivalence]] groups of many triangulated categories.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bapat |first1=Asilata |last2=Deopurkar |first2=Anand |last3=Licata |first3=Anthony M. |date=2023 |title=Spherical objects and stability conditions on 2-Calabi–Yau quiver categories |url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/s00209-022-03172-8 |journal=Mathematische Zeitschrift |language=en |volume=303 |issue=1 |article-number=13 |doi=10.1007/s00209-022-03172-8 |issn=0025-5874|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=":2">{{cite arXiv |last1=Hirano |first1=Yuki |title=Stability Conditions for 3-fold Flops |date=2022-11-02 |eprint=1907.09742 |last2=Wemyss |first2=Michael |class=math.AG }}</ref><ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Ishii |first1=Akira |title=Stability conditions on $A_n$-singularities |date=2010-04-19 |last2=Ueda |first2=Kazushi |last3=Uehara |first3=Hokuto |eprint=math/0609551 }}</ref> ''Wall-crossing,'' i.e. the analysis of how moduli spaces of semistable objects change as the stability condition varies in the stability manifold, has been employed to solve problems in [[enumerative geometry]] and [[Brill–Noether theory|Brill-Noether theory]].<ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Bayer |first1=Arend |title=The unreasonable effectiveness of wall-crossing in algebraic geometry |date=2022-01-10 |eprint=2201.03654 |last2=Macrì |first2=Emanuele |class=math.AG }}</ref><ref>{{cite arXiv |last=Toda |first=Yukinobu |title=Curve counting theories via stable objects I. DT/PT correspondence |date=2009 |class=math.AG |eprint=0902.4371 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Feyzbakhsh |first=Soheyla |date=2020-08-01 |title=Mukai's program (reconstructing a K3 surface from a curve) via wall-crossing |url=https://www.degruyterbrill.com/document/doi/10.1515/crelle-2019-0025/html |journal=Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik (Crelles Journal) |language=en |volume=2020 |issue=765 |pages=101–137 |doi=10.1515/crelle-2019-0025 |arxiv=1710.06692 |issn=1435-5345}}</ref>

==Definition and first examples==

=== Motivation ===
To construct well-behaved moduli spaces of [[Vector bundles on algebraic curves|vector bundles]] on a smooth [[algebraic curve]], it is necessary to restrict attention to the class of [[semistable vector bundle]]s—these are bundles <math>W</math> that satisfy the inequality <math>\mu(W)\geq \mu(V)</math> for all sub-bundles <math>V\subset W</math>, where <math>\mu(-)=\operatorname{deg}(-)/\operatorname{rank}(-)</math>is the slope function. This inequality of slopes can be equivalently stated by saying the [[complex number]] <math>Z(W)=-\operatorname{deg}(W)+i\operatorname{rank}(W)</math> has a greater [[Argument of a complex number|argument]] than analogously defined <math>Z(V)</math>.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Bayer |first=Arend |date=2011 |title=A tour to stability conditions on derived categories |url=https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~abayer/dc-lecture-notes.pdf }}</ref>

The [[Harder-Narasimhan filtration|Harder--Narasimhan theorem]] states that every [[coherent sheaf]] on the curve admits a filtration by semistable vector bundles and [[Skyscraper sheaf|skyscraper sheaves]]. It follows that every complex of coherent sheaves in the [[derived category]] of the curve admits a filtration by shifts of semistable bundles and skyscraper sheaves.

A Bridgeland stability condition on a triangulated category is an abstraction of the above phenomenon. It picks out a class of semistable objects which provide building blocks for the category, and provides numerical criteria for determining when a given object is semistable.

=== Formal definition ===
A stability condition on a triangulated category <math>\mathcal{D}</math> is a [[Ordered pair|pair]] <math>(Z,\mathcal{P})</math> where the ''slicing'' <math>\mathcal{P}</math> is a collection of [[Full subcategory|full]] [[Additive category|additive subcategories]] <math>\mathcal{P}(\varphi)\subset\mathcal{D}</math> for each <math>\varphi\in \mathbb{R}</math>, and the ''central charge'' <math>Z\colon \mathsf{K}_0(\mathcal{D})\to \mathbb{C}</math> is a [[group homomorphism]] from the [[Grothendieck group]] of <math>\mathcal{D}</math> to the additive group of the complex numbers, satisfying the following condition:<ref name="bridgeland" /><ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite arXiv|last1=Macrì |first1=Emanuele |last2=Schmidt |first2=Benjamin |date=2016-07-05 |title=Lectures on Bridgeland Stability |class=math.AG |language=en |eprint=1607.01262}}</ref>

;Shift-periodicity
: An object <math>A</math> lies in <math>\mathcal{P}(\varphi)</math> [[if and only if]] <math>A[1]\in \mathcal{P}(\varphi+1)</math>.
;Right-orthogonality : If <math>A\in \mathcal{P}(\varphi_1)</math>, <math>B\in \mathcal{P}(\varphi_2)</math>, and  <math>\varphi_1 > \varphi_2</math>, then <math>\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)=0</math>.
;Compatibility of slicing and central charge
:For every <math>\varphi\in\mathbb{R}</math> and non-zero object <math>A\in\mathcal{P}(\varphi)</math>, there is a positive real number <math>m(A)</math> (called the ''mass'' of <math>A</math>) such that<math display="inline">Z(A)=m(A)\cdot e^{i\pi\varphi}</math>.
;Existence of Harder—Narasimhan filtrations: For every object <math>E\in \mathcal{D}</math> there exists a finite sequence of real numbers <math>\varphi_1>\varphi_2>\cdots>\varphi_n</math>, and objects <math>A_i\in \mathcal{P}(\varphi_i)</math> for each <math>i</math> sitting in the sequence of [[exact triangle]]s below.[[File:HN Filtration in triangulated category.png|frameless|600px|left]]

For a stability condition <math>\sigma=(Z,\mathcal{P})</math> and a real number <math>\varphi\in\mathbb{R}</math>, a non-zero object <math>A\in\mathcal{P}(\varphi)</math> is said to be <math>\sigma</math>-semistable of phase <math>\varphi</math> (or simply '''semistable'''). If it additionally has no proper non-zero [[Subobject|sub-objects]]  in <math>\mathcal{P}(\varphi)</math>, it is said to be '''stable'''''.''<ref name="bridgeland" /> Given an [[Interval (mathematics)|interval]] <math>I\subset\mathbb{R}</math>, it is typical to write <math>\mathcal{P}(I)</math> for the smallest extension-closed subcategory of <math>\mathcal{D}</math> containing all <math>\mathcal{P}(\varphi)</math> for <math>\varphi\in I</math>.

The four conditions above constitute Bridgeland's original definition of a stability condition. For most applications including the construction of the Bridgeland stability manifold, it is necessary to impose one of the additional constraints below.<ref name=":1" />

;Local finiteness
: There exists a real number <math>\varepsilon >0</math> such that for all <math>\varphi\in\mathbb{R}</math>, the [[quasi-abelian category]]<math display="inline">\mathcal{P}(\varphi-\varepsilon, \varphi+\varepsilon)</math>has finite length.

;Support property
: The central charge admits a factorisation <math>Z\colon \mathsf{K}_0(\mathcal{D})\xrightarrow{\;\lambda\;}\Lambda\xrightarrow{\;z\;} \mathbb{C}</math> where <math>\Lambda</math> is a [[free abelian group]] of finite [[Rank of an abelian group|rank]], such that for some (equivalently any) norm <math>\Vert \cdot \Vert</math> on <math>\Lambda\otimes\mathbb{R}</math>, there is a real number <math>C>0</math> such that the inequality <math>|Z(E)|\geq C\cdot \Vert \lambda(E) \Vert</math>holds for all semi-stable objects <math>E</math>. This is equivalent to the existence of a [[symmetric bilinear form]] <math>Q</math> on the [[vector space]] <math>\Lambda\otimes\mathbb{R}</math> such that <math>Q(\lambda[E],\lambda[E])\geq 0</math> for each semi-stable object <math>E\in\mathcal{D}</math>, and <math>Q(\ell, \ell)\leq 0</math> for each <math>\ell\in \ker(z)\subset \Lambda\otimes \mathbb{R}</math>.
:
: Bayer and Macrì showed the support property implies local finiteness, but the converse implication is generally false.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bayer |first1=Arend |last2=Macrì |first2=Emanuele |date=2011-11-01 |title=The space of stability conditions on the local projective plane |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/duke-mathematical-journal/volume-160/issue-2/The-space-of-stability-conditions-on-the-local-projective-plane/10.1215/00127094-1444249.full |journal=Duke Mathematical Journal |volume=160 |issue=2 |doi=10.1215/00127094-1444249 |arxiv=0912.0043 |issn=0012-7094}}</ref>

The support property was introduced by [[Maxim Kontsevich|Kontsevich]] and [[Yan Soibelman|Soibelman]], as an abstraction of the observation that when the metric on a three-dimensional Calabi-Yau manifold approaches the large volume limit, the integrals of harmonic forms ("norms") on [[special Lagrangian submanifold]]s ("stable objects") is [[Uniform boundedness|uniformly bounded]] by their volumes ("central charge") .<ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Kontsevich |first1=Maxim |title=Stability structures, motivic Donaldson-Thomas invariants and cluster transformations |date=2008-11-16 |last2=Soibelman |first2=Yan |class=math.AG |eprint=0811.2435 }}</ref>

Many authors include the support property in the definition of a stability condition, calling those without the support property '''pre-stability''' '''conditions''' instead.<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last=Bayer |first=Arend |date=2019 |title=A short proof of the deformation property of Bridgeland stability conditions |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/s00208-019-01900-w |journal=Mathematische Annalen |language=en |volume=375 |issue=3–4 |pages=1597–1613 |doi=10.1007/s00208-019-01900-w |issn=0025-5831|arxiv=1606.02169 }}</ref>

=== Stability conditions on curves ===
For a smooth projective curve <math>C</math>, the function <math>Z(-)=-\operatorname{deg}(-)+i\cdot \operatorname{rank}(-)</math> extends to a well-defined central charge <math>\mathsf{K}_0(\mathsf{D}^bC)\to \mathbb{C}</math> on the derived category of coherent sheaves on <math>C</math>.

Declaring <math>\mathcal{P}(1)</math> to be the full subcategory of torsion sheaves, <math>\mathcal{P}(\varphi)</math> for <math>\varphi\in (0,1)</math> to be the full additive subcategory generated by semistable vector bundles  <math>W</math> with slope <math>\mu(W)=-\tan(\varphi)</math>, and extending to remaining <math>\varphi\in \mathbb{R}</math> by shift-periodicity defines a slicing on <math>\mathsf{D}^b C</math> by the Harder—Narasimhan theorem.

The pair <math>(Z,\mathcal{P})</math> is a Bridgeland stability condition that has the support property. More generally, the construction can be repeated with any function <math>Z_w(-)=-\operatorname{deg}(-)+w\cdot \operatorname{rank}(-)</math>for a number <math>w</math> in the [[Upper half-plane|complex upper half-plane]] <math>\mathbb{H}</math>, each such pair <math>(Z_w,\mathcal{P}_w)</math> is a stability condition on <math>\mathsf{D}^bC</math>.<ref name=":0" />

== On abelian categories ==
A stability function on an [[abelian category]] <math>\mathcal{A}</math> is a group homomorphism <math>Z\colon \mathsf{K}_0(\mathcal{A})\to \mathbb{C}</math> such that for each non-zero object <math>E\in \mathcal{A}</math>, the complex number <math>Z(E)</math> lies in the semi-closed upper half plane <math>\mathbb{R}_{<0}\cup \mathbb{H}</math>.

The ''phase'' of <math>E</math> is the real number <math>\varphi(E)=\tfrac{1}{\pi}\operatorname{arg}Z(E)\in (0,1]</math>. The object <math>E</math> is ''semi-stable'' (resp. ''stable'') with respect to <math>Z</math> if for every proper non-zero sub-object <math>F\subset E</math>, the inequality <math>\varphi(F)\leq \varphi(E)</math> (resp. <math>\varphi(F)<\varphi(E)</math>) holds.

The stability function <math>Z</math> has the '''Harder—Narasimhan property''' if every non-zero object <math>E\in \mathcal{A}</math> admits a [[Filtration (mathematics)|filtration]] <math display="block">0=E_0\subset E_1\subset \cdots \subset E_n=E</math> such that each factor <math>F_i=E_i/E_{i-1}</math> is semistable and their phases satisfy <math display="inline">\varphi(F_1)>\varphi(F_2)>\ldots >\varphi(F_n).</math>

Bridgeland showed that a stability condition <math>(Z,\mathcal{P})</math> on a triangulated category <math>\mathcal{D}</math> is equivalent to the data of the heart of a [[T-structure|bounded t-structure]] <math>\mathcal{A}\subset\mathcal{D}</math>, and a stability function <math>Z\colon \mathsf{K}_0(\mathcal{A})\to \mathbb{C}</math> with the Harder—Narasimhan property.<ref name="bridgeland" /> There is a natural isomorphism of Grothendieck groups <math>\mathsf{K}_0(\mathcal{A})\cong \mathsf{K}_0(\mathcal{D})</math> that turns the stability function into a central charge, and defining <math display="block">\mathcal{P}(\varphi)=\left\langle E\in \mathcal{A}\;|\; E\text{ semi-stable with }\varphi(E)=\varphi \right\rangle</math>for <math>\varphi\in (0,1]</math> uniquely specifies a slicing on <math>\mathcal{D}</math>. Conversely if  <math>(Z,\mathcal{P})</math> is a stability condition, then the subcategory  <math display="inline">\mathcal{P}(0,1]</math>is the heart of a bounded t-structure on which <math>Z</math> gives a stability function with Harder—Narasimhan property.

== The stability manifold ==
For an [[Small category|essentially small]] triangulated category <math>\mathcal{D}</math> with a fixed [[Surjective function|surjection]] <math>\lambda\colon \mathsf{K}_0(\mathcal{D})\to \Lambda</math> onto a free abelian group of finite rank, there is a complex manifold <math>\operatorname{Stab}(\mathcal{D})</math> called the ''stability manifold'' whose points parametrise stability conditions <math>(Z,\mathcal{P})</math> on <math>\mathcal{D}</math> for which the central charge <math>Z</math> factors through <math>\lambda</math> and has the support property with respect to this factorisation.<ref name=":3" />

Specifically, all stability conditions (with or without the support property) form a [[metric space]]. This space is naturally equipped with a [[Continuous function|continuous map]] <math>(Z,P)\mapsto Z</math> to the Euclidean space <math>\operatorname{Hom}_\mathbb{Z}(\mathsf{K}_0\mathcal{D},\mathbb{C})</math>. When restricted to the subset <math>\operatorname{Stab}(\mathcal{D})</math> of stability conditions that have the support property with respect to <math>\Lambda</math>, this map is a [[local homeomorphism]] [[onto]] the subspace <math>\operatorname{Hom}_\mathbb{Z}(\Lambda,\mathbb{C})</math>. This is known as '''Bridgeland's''' '''deformation property''', and gives <math>\operatorname{Stab}(\mathcal{D})</math> the structure of a <math>\operatorname{rank}(\Lambda)</math>-dimensional complex manifold.<ref name="bridgeland" /><ref name=":0" />

=== Group actions ===
The group of autoequivalences of <math>\mathcal{D}</math> has a [[left action]] on the stability manifold <math>\operatorname{Stab}(\mathcal{D})</math>, where the equivalence <math>\Phi\colon \mathcal{D}\to \mathcal{D}</math> acts by the [[isometry]] <math>\Phi\cdot (Z,\mathcal{P})=(Z\circ \Phi^{-1}, \Phi\circ \mathcal{P})</math>. In many situations this action is via [[deck transformations]] of the local homeomorphism <math>\mathcal{Z}\colon \operatorname{Stab}(\mathcal{D})\to \operatorname{Hom}_\mathbb{Z}(\Lambda, \mathbb{C})</math>, thus providing a topological tool for the analysis of autoequivalences of <math>\mathcal{D}</math>.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Bridgeland |first=Tom |title=Stability Conditions and Kleinian Singularities |journal=International Mathematics Research Notices |date=2005 |doi=10.1093/imrn/rnp081 |language=en |arxiv=math/0508257 }}</ref><ref name=":2" />

The neutral component <math>\mathsf{GL}^+(2,\mathbb{R})</math> of the [[general linear group]], containing matrices with positive determinant, has a right action on <math>\mathbb{C}</math> and hence on the space <math>\operatorname{Hom}_\mathbb{Z}(\Lambda, \mathbb{C})</math>. This action lifts over the local homeomorphism <math>\mathcal{Z}</math> to a right action of [[universal cover]] <math>\tilde\mathsf{GL}{}^+(2,\mathbb{R})</math> on <math>\operatorname{Stab}(\mathcal{D})</math>. The additive group <math>\mathbb{C}</math> is a [[subgroup]] of <math>\tilde\mathsf{GL}{}^+(2,\mathbb{R})</math>, and can be seen as the universal cover of the multiplicative group <math>\mathbb{C}^\ast\subset \mathsf{GL}(2,\mathbb{R})</math>. The induced action of <math>\mathbb{C}</math> on <math>\operatorname{Stab}(\mathcal{D})</math>, called the '''rotation action'',''''' is explicitly given by <math>(Z,\mathcal{P})\cdot (x+iy)=(e^{-i\pi (x+iy)} Z, \mathcal{P}(x+\cdot ))</math>.<ref name="bridgeland" />

=== Geometric stability conditions ===
When <math>\mathcal{D}</math> is the derived category of coherent sheaves on an [[Smooth scheme|smooth]] and [[Proper variety|proper]] [[algebraic variety]] <math>X</math>, the group <math>\Lambda</math> is typically taken to be the ''numerical Grothendieck group'' <math>\mathsf{K}_\text{num}(X)</math>, defined as the quotient of <math>\mathsf{K}_0(\mathcal{D})</math> by the [[Kernel (linear algebra)|kernel]] of the [[Euler characteristic of a sheaf|Euler pairing]] <math display="block">\chi(E,F)=\sum_i (-1)^i \operatorname{dim}\operatorname{Hom}(E,F[i]).</math>A stability condition that has the support property with respect to <math>\mathsf{K}_\text{num}(X)</math> is called ''numerical.'' <ref name=":4">{{Cite arXiv|last=Rekuski |first=Nick |date=2023-10-16 |title=Contractibility of the geometric stability manifold of a surface |class=math.AG |language=en |eprint=2310.10499}}</ref>

A '''geometric stability condition''' on <math>\mathcal{D}</math> is a numerical stability condition <math>(Z,\mathcal{P})</math> for which all skyscraper sheaves <math>\mathcal{O}_p</math> at closed points <math>p\in X</math>are semistable and have the same phase, that is, there is a real number <math>\varphi</math> such that <math>\{\mathcal{O}_p\;|\; p\in X\}\subset \mathcal{P}(\varphi)</math>.<ref name=":4" /> An example of geometric stability condition is the one defined by slope stability on a smooth curve.

In 2026, [[Chunyi Li]] established the existence of geometric stability conditions on smooth projective varieties.<ref>{{Cite arXiv|last=Li |first=Chunyi |date=2026-01-30 |title=A Remark on Stability Conditions on Smooth Projective Varieties |class=math.AG |language=en |eprint=2601.22994}}</ref>

== Examples ==

=== Elliptic curves ===
There is an analysis by Bridgeland for the case of elliptic curves. He finds<ref name="bridgeland" /><ref>{{cite arXiv |last=Uehara |first=Hokuto |date=2015-11-18 |title=Autoequivalences of derived categories of elliptic surfaces with non-zero Kodaira dimension |eprint=1501.06657 |pages=10–12|class=math.AG }}</ref> there is an equivalence<blockquote><math>\text{Stab}(X)/\text{Aut}(X) \cong \text{GL}^+(2,\mathbb{R})/\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})</math></blockquote>where <math>\text{Stab}(X)</math> is the set of stability conditions and <math>\text{Aut}(X)</math> is the set of autoequivalences of the derived category <math>D^b(X)</math>.
